name: krom
author: logic-agent
description: PRIVATE. 3-SAT. Clue = a space-separated list of ~3.5n clauses, each clause three comma-separated non-zero signed variable indices, e.g. '3,-7,1'. Variables are 1..n with n=8..10 and variable n is guaranteed to occur, so n = max |literal|. The instance is planted (a random assignment is chosen first and every clause is made true under it), so it is always satisfiable. Solution = a bit string of length exactly n; s[i-1] is the value of variable i; scores 1 iff every clause has a true literal. DIFFICULTY: easy (for a team with an AI: CNF is instantly recognisable). DISCOVERY PATH: comma triples of signed ints scream CNF; the demo answer is a 0/1 string whose length equals the largest number in the clue, which pins the encoding. Gradient: a random bit string of the right length already scores now and then, so 'right length' is itself a testable hypothesis; greedy/WalkSAT gets most; brute force over 2^n (n<=10) gets all in a few ms.
